en.title: Hormuz Traffic Hopes Rise After US Ship Passage
en.summary: The probability for Strait of Hormuz traffic returning to normal by end of May surged 15% to 30%. This increase was primarily driven by the successful passage of two American merchant ships through the Strait on May 4, 2026, signaling potential de-escalation or successful navigation strategies.
drivers: US merchant ships successfully transited Strait.
Demonstration of US capability to secure passage.
Increased feasibility of limited commercial shipping.
en.why_matters: The Strait of Hormuz is a critical chokepoint for global oil shipments, and its disruption significantly impacts energy prices and global trade. A return to normal traffic would alleviate supply concerns and stabilize markets.
en.bull_case: Successful, albeit escorted, transit of US merchant ships proves limited traffic can resume, paving the way for more by May end.
en.bear_case: Iran's resumed attacks and Trump's mission hold suggest ongoing escalation, making normal traffic by May end unlikely.
